description: THE NAME-2 REVISION GOLDEN (docs/AUDIT-PRODUCT.md S-24/S-24b). This is fillet-top-edge-40x25x10-r5 AFTER the edit every engineer makes: the sketch's 40 mm width is retyped to 55, and the fillet's stored EdgeSignature STILL names the 40 mm edge — end_b (40,0,10), midpoint (20,0,10), length 40 — exactly the state a document is left in when a dimension is changed and nothing re-picks the reference. The strict stage-1 matcher pins both endpoints, the midpoint AND the length, so all four fields are now stale and the picked edge was orphaned (subshape_unresolved) by the FIRST such edit, taking every feature below it with it. Resolution goes through the tier-2 durable re-match (geometry.kernel.edges.collinear_overlapping_match): the edge's SUPPORTING LINE and the overlap of its span are invariant under the edge growing along itself, which is what the audit meant by 'the same boundary edge of the same face, just longer'. The gate is not merely that it rebuilds — it is that the rounded edge is the 55 mm front-top edge and NOT one of its three sharp top neighbours, which the centroid and the surface area both witness. Sibling of revise-thickness-hole-on-moved-face-60x40x16 (the FACE half of the same problem); together they lock both subshape kinds against the commonest revision in CAD.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, cross-checked against the harness (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). Base body is a 55x25x10 box; ONE convex 90-degree edge — the front-top edge, along x, now length L=55 — is rounded at r=5.

volume: a convex 90-degree fillet removes r^2*(1 - pi/4) per unit length (a square corner r^2 becomes a quarter disc pi*r^2/4 in cross-section). Over L=55: removed = 55*25*(1 - pi/4) = 1375 - 343.75*pi. volume = 13750 - 1375 + 343.75*pi = 12375 + 343.75*pi = 13454.922474671492 mm^3 (measured deviation 1.8e-12).

surface_area: unchanged faces — bottom 55*25 = 1375, back(+Y) 55*10 = 550. Narrowed planar faces — top loses a 5 mm strip along the filleted edge -> 55*20 = 1100; front(-Y) loses a 5 mm strip -> 55*5 = 275. The two end faces (x=0, x=55) each lose the rounded corner at (y=0,z=10): 250 - 25*(1 - pi/4) = 225 + 25*pi/4 apiece. Fillet lateral (quarter cylinder r=5, length 55) = pi*r*L/2 = 137.5*pi.

centroid.x = 27.5 exactly: the body keeps the mirror symmetry perpendicular to the filleted edge, and 27.5 (not the stored signature's midpoint x=20) is itself an assertion that the fillet followed the edge to its NEW extent instead of stopping at the stale 40.

centroid.y and .z are INDEPENDENT OF L and therefore identical to fillet-top-edge-40x25x10-r5's, which is a free cross-check of both goldens: the removed region is a prism along x whose cross-section S does not change with length, so y = (W*H*(W/2) - A_S*y_S)/(W*H - A_S) with the L cancelling top and bottom. S = square [0,5]x[5,10] minus the quarter disc (r=5, centre (5,5)); A_S = 25 - 25*pi/4; quarter-disc centroid offset 4r/(3*pi) = 20/(3*pi) from its centre toward the quadrant. centroid.y = 12.749642075576444 mm, centroid.z = 4.914839098070588 mm (measured deviations 1.8e-15 and 0.0).

bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[55,25,10]: the fillet is tangent to the front face at z=5 and to the top face at y=5, and spans the full x extent. max.x = 55 is the second witness that the reference re-anchored to the GROWN edge — a body built from the stale 40 could not reach it.

topology: 7 faces (6 box + 1 quarter-cylinder fillet), 15 edges (13 straight + 2 quarter arcs where the fillet meets the end faces), 1 shell — unchanged from the 40 mm original, because the edit changed a length and no topology. A tier-2 match that had re-anchored onto a DIFFERENT edge would still give 7/15/1, which is why the mass properties above (not the counts) carry the correctness claim.

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular 0.1 rad, isRelative=False): each fillet quarter-arc discretizes to 2*ceil((pi/2)/0.1) = 32 segments, the same 2x-angular-estimate rule the fillet goldens exhibit; the closed form from fillet-top-edge-40x25x10-r5 is nodes = 26 + 4*N and triangles = 12 + 4*N, and it carries NO L term — a cylindrical face is ruled along its length, so a longer face needs no extra division to meet the linear deflection. Predicted 154 / 140 at N=32, measured 154 / 140.

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned: asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on glTF-writer upgrades without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: CURVED-GEOMETRY tolerance, inherited from fillet-top-edge-40x25x10-r5 (the same single quarter-cylinder fillet face through OCCT's Gauss-quadrature integration in GProp) and re-measured on THIS body rather than copied blindly: volume 1.8e-12 mm^3, surface_area 9.1e-13 mm^2, centroid <= 1.8e-15 mm, AABB <= 8.9e-16 mm. The documented 1e-9 ceiling is ~5e2x the observed worst case, with headroom for libm/platform variation in the quadrature across CI hosts. The tier-2 re-match contributes ZERO error by construction — it selects a kernel Edge, it does not derive a position from the stored signature (contrast the FACE resolver, whose resilient tiers must re-anchor a plane origin). Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
